title: Michael Simpson: Why Child Safety Breaks Standard AI Safety—and How We Can Fix It

the authors of the paper preventing

about the scale of this problem.

Exploited Children,
or NCMEC, is the US clearinghouse for
this sort of abuse material. That means

More than 29 million images, more than
26 million videos.

on professional networking sites, it's
on music streaming platforms. Everyone

AI is entering.

more than 400,000 reports
uh were went to NCMEC that that

Internet Watch Foundation, which is the
UK's hotline, their clearinghouse,
saw a 154% increase in photorealistic
generative AI material reported to them.

misconception.
Just because the images are real or fake
doesn't mean that the victims are.
So, this causes three harms to real
kids. First, it hides real victims. So,
one of the ways that we deal with this
material is we prioritize things that
haven't been seen before. If an image
has been circulating in a fender
community for 15 years, it usually
doesn't mean that there's active abuse

new images.

images entering the system, and it makes
it really hard for investigators to
prioritize which cases to look at. So,
there's investigators looking for kids
who don't exist, and the kids who really
need help aren't getting it.
Second, it revictimizes existing
victims. So, their abuse material is
recirculated, it's reimagined,
intensified. There are lures devoted to
recreating images of individual children
floating around.
Third, it creates new victims uh through
things like sexual extortion, coercion,
bullying. I think we've all heard about
this happening at schools. So, kids are
really getting hurt by this. And AI
platforms are aware of this, and that's
why most of the major AI platforms and
tech companies came together with Thorn
to develop a framework called Safety by
Design that has concrete mitigations
that we can implement today.
And this was really effective. Uh it
turned into an IEEE standard that was
approved last week and should be
published in two or three months. Uh and
it was built to be extensible and
future-looking because core components

effective. We should be doing this now,
but it needs some pieces. And it needs
some pieces for a good reason.

here. So, on the one side you have AI
providers, they have the models, they
They telemetry, they have the resources

and legally they shouldn't and they
can't. Uh

constraints.

there are certain cases when platforms

like a major concern.
Uh second evaluation, it is illegal to

environment. Any safeguards that we put
into place, offenders will work to
uh to work around them and overcome
uh any anything we do. And finally, this
is really wellness heavy for the people
doing this work.
And so, those four constraints lead to
these 15 open problems.
They span the model life cycle from
design to deployment to maintenance.
Uh I'm going to go through every single
one of these, but I'm going to spend a
little bit of extra time on A2 and B4
because I have case studies there to

So, let's start with the data.

that you can only do probabilistic

trained that we clean the data set

We have another problem.

set,

Sam.
Uh you have images of children and

concern is that it could fuse these. So,
best practice in safety by design today
is to not train a data set with both of
those concepts. But, it would be better
if we could restrain the space so that
you couldn't fuse those concepts, but
you could still have both concepts in
the data set.
We also need to resist harmful
fine-tuning. So, fine-tuning is great.
We should be specializing models for the
tasks that they do, but fine-tuning in

Uh automated methods are usually less

and better research into what is
effective here.
We know things like gray scaling and

effective, but we need more research on
this problem.
And finally,
when safeguards fail, we need better

So, we need things that are robust to uh

thing that something that's difficult to
add after the fact.

persist through that.

they have guides, they share tips, and

platforms do have access to things like

what

meets the standards that we need.

to prevent the automation of grooming

with these agents. And
